category_title: Primary students with low reading motivation who perceive a lack of autonomy and environmental discomfort
minimal_context: The student is participating in an independent reading task in a pullout reading intervention room.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's get started with our independent reading. Please sit in your regular chair and begin your book.

STUDENT: This chair is uncomfortable. I would prefer to spend more time reading in the comfy blue chair. And it's a little bit noisier in here than my classroom.

TUTOR: Just sit there for today and try to focus on your reading.

STUDENT: It's harder to read in here. The school should install an insulated pod in this room so I can have a quiet place to read.

TUTOR: Okay, please stop reading your book now so we can do spelling and sounds.

STUDENT: My classroom teacher doesn’t stop us when we’re reading to do spelling or to do sounds and stuff. I don't get to make much decisions in here.

options.A: Regularly monitor the student's motivation specific to the reading intervention and modify instruction in accordance with the findings.
options.B: Place an exclusive display board in the intervention room only for the student to display their independent reading work.
options.C: Provide individual storage space in the intervention room, such as chair bags or desks with compartments, for reading materials.
options.D: Provide the student with access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation, such as a squishy stress-relief ball.
